video_title: Crypto Funeral, CZ vs. Star, Bring Back Jensen? - The Chopping Block
gist: The Chopping Block holds a 'crypto funeral' with FalconX's Josh Lim: BTC at 65K, $2B of liquidations, a $20B stablecoin contraction and rate-hike fears, blamed on hidden leverage (BTC hedges, levered DATs, HYPE reflexivity) and capital rotating into the Anthropic IPO, with recovery seen around Jan-Feb. The panel also debates the CZ vs. Star blame feud and mostly argues against bringing back Jensen Huang at Nvidia, citing mounting US government and export-control pressure.

insights.claim: Crypto suffered a brutal week: BTC fell to 65K after touching 62K, over $2B of mostly-long liquidations, six straight red weeks (-23% since the Nov 4 local high), ~$2B of spot ETF outflows, ETH at $1,800, SOL under $80 and fear & greed at 10.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Extreme fear (index 10) alongside forced long liquidations is classic capitulation territory; watch ETF flows for a turn.
insights.quote: The fear and greed index is at 10.

insights.claim: Stablecoin supply contracted by roughly $20B, one of the first contractions in a long time, undermining the 'prices down but fundamentals up' bull argument for this cycle.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Stablecoin growth was the key fundamental support narrative; its reversal removes a pillar and signals capital leaving crypto rails.

insights.claim: Fed rate-hike odds are at 92% after a hot CPI print, adding a macro headwind to crypto.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A hiking Fed is a direct headwind to risk assets; crypto rallies likely need hikes priced and cleared.

insights.claim: Robinhood Chain's TVL has held up relatively well, but the meme coins and stock tokens trading on it are down 80-90% in many cases, so retail 'trenches' activity has been decimated.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Sticky TVL with collapsing token prices suggests infrastructure usage persists while speculative long-tail assets are wiped out.

insights.claim: Situational Awareness's 13F showed a ~92% decline between Q2 and Q3 (the 13F excludes private positions such as Anthropic and may include redemptions), a striking drawdown signal outside crypto.
insights.speaker: Tarun
insights.so_what: Severe AI-fund drawdowns show risk-off spreading across AI and crypto; contrarians compare it to Multicoin's -91% year before a big rebound.

insights.claim: Crypto's selloff looks like a delayed catch-up to the AI complex, where many names are down 25-40% from highs of a few months ago.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Crypto and AI risk capital are trading as one correlated bucket; AI equity stabilization may lead crypto.

themes.theme: Why it's selling: flows, leverage and hedges

insights.claim: FalconX saw hidden leverage build up: Bitcoin open interest hit range highs a week or two before the crash, largely as beta hedges for illiquid altcoin portfolios expressed in BTC because altcoin liquidity is abysmal and market makers have bowed out.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: When alt liquidity dries up, BTC becomes the hedge vehicle and absorbs outsized selling; BTC OI spikes can precede liquidation cascades.

insights.claim: A notable FalconX desk trade was up to ~$40M of premium spent on IBIT puts into year-end, struck around the equivalent of $55-60K BTC.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Large put positioning at 55-60K marks where sophisticated money sees downside risk and may create dealer-hedging pressure near those levels.
insights.quote: up to like $40 million of premium was spent on puts into end of year

insights.claim: Clients are using Bitcoin as a weekend proxy to hedge macro risk such as China-Taiwan military headlines, because traditional markets offer no liquidity on weekends.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: BTC trades as the only 24/7 macro hedge, so geopolitical weekend headlines can produce outsized BTC moves.

insights.claim: Weekend selling was concentrated in Bitcoin on Coinbase: FalconX research shows roughly 2-3x normal weekend activity for BTC versus about 1-1.5x for alts, pointing to specific sellers rather than broad panic.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Concentration in Coinbase BTC flow hints at US corporate/DAT sellers rather than broad retail panic.

insights.claim: Hidden leverage extends to digital asset treasury companies (DATs): some levered DAT vehicles have debt payments coming due and some are being removed from indices, with Nakamoto cited as potentially needing a debt restructuring while Strategy has a relatively clean capital structure.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Distinguish DATs by capital structure; levered treasuries facing maturities are forced sellers.
insights.quote: the ghost of the dats coming back

insights.claim: Capital is rotating out of crypto into the Anthropic IPO, semiconductors and other beaten-down sectors; the Zapo CEO reportedly sees investors selling Bitcoin to raise cash for Anthropic because it is their most liquid risk asset.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim / Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Large IPOs can drain liquid crypto holdings near-term, though with the IPO around $60B+ this can't explain all the selling.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is just more liquid than a lot of the other stuff that they have in their portfolios

insights.claim: The HYPE drawdown was driven by reflexive leverage: traders borrowed USDC against HYPE to top up long perp positions, with one $50-60M position near liquidation at $58; since the largest Hype traders are also the largest holders, they must sell on the way down.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: HYPE is highly reflexive; liquid funds are buying it back as a top holding, making it a high-beta rebound candidate.
insights.quote: it's like the most reflexive asset out there

insights.claim: The Binance hack likely had little net effect on BTC/ETH since Binance needed only a couple hundred million to cover reserves, but was net negative for affected alts because buybacks from foundations increase circulating float; the actual selling was North Korea swapping stolen assets to ETH.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Hacked alts face float expansion from foundation buybacks; fade bounces premised on Binance covering losses.

themes.theme: CZ vs. Star: blame wars over the selloff

insights.claim: CZ attributed the BTC decline to ETF outflows, hot inflation, the midterms, AI/security fears and the Anthropic IPO drawing capital, and denied Binance sold tokens, saying he was buying with fresh stables.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Exchange leaders' public narratives are self-interested; rely on flow data rather than founder claims.

insights.claim: OKX CEO Star accused CZ of lying and blamed Binance for the market's declines, echoing his earlier claim that Binance caused the 10/10 record liquidation day; the panel found the claim that Binance is pushing the market down implausible.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim / Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Exchange feuds create headline noise but are not evidence of systematic selling.

themes.theme: Outlook: rate hikes, malaise and the next catalyst

insights.claim: Josh Lim expects about a one-month malaise with end-of-year (and possibly Q1) Fed hikes plus political uncertainty around Elizabeth Warren, with market comfort returning around January-February, possibly after only a brief Santa Claus rally.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Don't rush to buy the dip; a sustainable re-entry window is seen in Jan-Feb after hikes are digested.
insights.quote: it's going to sort of play out closer to Jan Feb time frame

insights.claim: Repositioning after the 'blue wave' election is preventing aggressive dip-buying in crypto.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Political regime change is a structural overhang for crypto policy expectations.

insights.claim: Tom argues the defining mood is apathy rather than panic, with many voices having left crypto, and the core unanswered question is what catalyst brings the next incremental buyer, since adoption (stablecoin volumes still rising) has decoupled from asset prices.
insights.speaker: Tom
insights.so_what: Without a narrative tying usage growth back to token prices, rallies may lack incremental buyers.
insights.quote: stable coin market cap going down but stable coin volumes are still keep going up

insights.claim: Every deep bear market feels uniquely final, so there is no phenomenological evidence this bear is different in kind from 2018-19 or 2022.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Capitulation-feel is common to all bottoms; treat it as a contrarian signal rather than proof of terminal decline.
insights.quote: I've never been in a bare market that was like this one is obviously short-term.

insights.claim: Tarun disputes that past bears lacked narratives, citing 2018-19 when L1s like Polkadot raised abroad after being shunned in the US and were then marked up 1000x post-pandemic.
insights.speaker: Tarun
insights.so_what: Sectors shunned in bear markets can become the next cycle's leaders.

insights.claim: The Dragonfly host expects the next decade to be existing crypto categories growing larger rather than net-new breakthroughs, with Bitcoin ownership broadening, conditional on getting through quantum and AI risks.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Favors compounding of incumbent winners over hunting new categories; quantum is a flagged tail risk.

insights.claim: Dragonfly is invested in Pearl, an adaptation of proof of work for the AI era, on the thesis that energy will increasingly go to AI compute rather than being wasted on Bitcoin mining.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Signals a view that Bitcoin's energy-based security model competes with AI compute for power.

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO as a crypto catalyst

insights.claim: Pre-IPO Anthropic perps on Trade XYZ imply about $1.6-1.7T (fully diluted), with the Binance perp about 43% off its ~$2T high, versus a reported 6x-oversubscribed IPO range of $1.3-1.4T.
insights.speaker: Tarun / Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Pre-IPO RWA perps use inconsistent share-count conventions, so compare implied valuations carefully.

insights.claim: A strong Anthropic IPO is argued to be good for crypto because it implies AI diffusing through a growing economy, and because newly liquid Anthropic employees are likelier than 401k/institutional sellers to deploy into crypto and Bitcoin, though only after unlocks around April-May.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Mark the post-IPO unlock window (~6 months) as a potential crypto inflow catalyst.

insights.claim: Josh Lim expects the Anthropic IPO to follow SpaceX's path: a banker-priced first-day pop, then a slow bleed over about six months as traders hedge ahead of employee share selling.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Treat the first-day pop as a fade candidate; anticipate supply from aggressive unlock schedules.
insights.quote: we just see a slow bleed out of that stock after the first day pop

insights.claim: Anthropic's unlock schedule is more aggressive than SpaceX's and far from the standard 180-day lockup, resembling crypto token vesting curves, though overwhelming demand likely makes it a non-issue for Anthropic.
insights.speaker: Panelist
insights.so_what: Crypto-style vesting analysis now applies to mega-IPOs; model staged unlock supply rather than a single 180-day cliff.
insights.quote: SpaceX bringing the weirdness back. Anthropic is really bringing the weirdness back.

themes.theme: Jensen Huang exit and Nvidia's political risk

insights.claim: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid a reported affair with Alice Wong (alleged spy) and a second affair with direct report Kimberly Powell; the CFO is interim CEO, and ARM's CEO (transcribed as Renee Hos) is reported as front-runner.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: CEO succession uncertainty at the world's most valuable company is a key AI-complex risk factor.

insights.claim: The Commerce Department began enforcing restrictions on chip rentals by Chinese companies in neoclouds in Malaysia, Singapore and Japan, with congressional hearings being called, signaling a crackdown on Nvidia's China/Southeast Asia channels.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Tightening export enforcement hits Nvidia demand and Southeast Asian neocloud operators.

insights.claim: On Polymarket, Jensen was at 85% to keep his job before the second affair was revealed, and the second affair swung the odds sharply toward replacement.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Prediction markets offer a real-time gauge of governance events.

insights.claim: Tarun argues Nvidia will be fine for ~2 years but risks losing strategic direction in 5-7 years without Jensen, since his risky bets (making GPUs for crypto miners, buying Mellanox for an interconnect advantage over AMD) kept CUDA dominant, while replacement candidates look conservative.
insights.speaker: Tarun
insights.so_what: Long-horizon Nvidia holders should weigh the loss of founder-driven risk-taking beyond the near term.

insights.claim: Nvidia losing market share is overdetermined regardless of Jensen, because customers are building competing hardware and Anthropic's filings state it can replicate its Nvidia workloads on AMD.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Structural share loss to customer silicon and AMD is a long-term Nvidia headwind independent of leadership.
insights.quote: Nvidia losing market share is overdetermined.

insights.claim: The bigger Nvidia risk is the united fury of the US government rather than losing Jensen: incoming Democrats are angry over Nvidia's lobbying against chip export controls, and the midterms showed the public strongly anti-AI and against selling chips to China.
insights.speaker: Host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Expect heavier export regulation and political scrutiny on Nvidia and AI; tech calls to reinstate Jensen look miscalibrated.
insights.quote: What's coming to Nvidia is like the fury of the United States government

insights.claim: A piece from an AI research group (transcribed as EPAI) claiming statistical fingerprinting proves DeepSeek 4.1 was trained on GB300s appeared days after the affair news, which a panelist reads as Anthropic and OpenAI (now in favor of export controls) welcoming Nvidia's setback.
insights.speaker: Josh Lim
insights.so_what: Frontier labs' alignment on export controls increases regulatory pressure on Nvidia's China sales.
